newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SANITAS 1Q PROFIT DIPS, PRODUCTION UP.
newsitem.headline: SANITAS 1Q PROFIT DIPS, PRODUCTION UP.

text.p: Lithuania's largest producer of pharmaceutical products, Sanitas, said on Tuesday that its 1Q net profit was 2.2 million litas versus 2.9 million litas last year.
The company's production for the first quarter rose to 11.8 million litas from 10.9 million litas last year, the company's general director, Albertas Bertulis, told Reuters.
"Our profit fell a bit because the government cancelled our profit tax privileges, and this quarter we had to pay 29 percent profit tax," he said.
He also said that the firm's Russian partners only got their licenses for Lithuanian medicine in February, a factor which almost "brought sales to a halt in January."
The company exports 90 percent of its production, 75 percent of it to Russia.
Bertulis said that the company was targeting other CIS markets.
He added that the company's net profit for the second quarter was expected to be about the same as the first quarter results.
The company's net profit in 1996 was over ten million litas.

The company's shares are registered on the A list of the Vilnius bourse but trade in them was suspended on Tuesday for up to three months while the firm increases its authorized capital from reserves.
Dealers said on Tuesday that one of the company's major shareholders was looking to sell their shares.
